## Claims
- [proved] For \(t\in\mathbb Z\), let \(P(t)=0\) if \(t<0\), and, for \(t=6u+r\ge0\) with \(0\le r<6\), set
  \[
  P(t)=
  \begin{cases}
  3u^2+3u+1,&r=0,\\
  3u^2+4u+1,&r=1,\\
  3u^2+5u+2,&r=2,\\
  3u^2+6u+3,&r=3,\\
  3u^2+7u+4,&r=4,\\
  3u^2+8u+5,&r=5.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  Then \(P(t)=\#\{\lambda:\ell(\lambda)\le3,\ |\lambda|=t\}\).
- [proved] For \(b\ge1\), put \(R_b(N)=\#\{\rho\subseteq b^3:|\rho|=N\}\). Its complete piecewise quasi-polynomial formula is
  \[
  R_b(N)=
  \begin{cases}
  0,&N<0\text{ or }N>3b,\\[2pt]
  P(N),&0\le N\le b,\\[2pt]
  P(N)-P(N-b-1)-P(N-b-2)-P(N-b-3),
    &b<N\le\lfloor3b/2\rfloor,\\[2pt]
  R_b(3b-N),&\lfloor3b/2\rfloor<N\le3b.
  \end{cases}
  \]
- [proved] The complement \(\rho^\vee=(b-\rho_3,b-\rho_2,b-\rho_1)\) is an involution of partitions in \(b^3\) and gives
  \[
  R_b(N)=R_b(3b-N).
  \]
- [proved] Conditional on the accepted graded integral basis \(Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^3}\mathbb Z e_\rho\), \(\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|\), one has
  \[
  \operatorname{rank}Q_{ij+N}=R_b(N),\qquad
  Q_{ij+N}=0\quad(N\notin[0,3b]),
  \]
  and every \(Q_{ij+N}\) is free abelian, hence torsion-free.

## Strategy
The rectangle generating function is
\[
\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^3}q^{|\rho|}
=\binom{b+3}{3}_q
=\frac{(1-q^{b+1})(1-q^{b+2})(1-q^{b+3})}
{(1-q)(1-q^2)(1-q^3)}.
\]
The denominator coefficient is \(P(N)\). For \(N\le\lfloor3b/2\rfloor<2b+3\), no product of two numerator terms contributes, yielding the second nontrivial piece. Complementation supplies the remaining degrees.

Thus the requested target is established relative to the accepted graded-basis hypothesis.

## Gaps
The torsion-freeness assertion uses the accepted integral graded-basis statement; it is not independently reproved here.
